newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends near unchanged in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends near unchanged in slow trade.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended near unchanged Wednesday as the market lacked enough steam to break out of recent ranges, sources said.
May finished 0.1 cent lower at $1.883 per mmBtu after wavering between $1.86 and $1.92. June settled down 0.2 cent at $1.928, while other deferreds were narrowly mixed.
"The market was just waiting for the AGAs. Other than that there was really no reason for it to move very much since cash was pretty flat and volume has been light," one Houston-based source said.

Support in May at $1.86 remained secure, but traders pegged next support at Monday's low of $1.825 and at $1.78 and the contract low of $1.71. Resistance was still seen at $1.92, and then at $1.95 and last Thursday's high of $1.97. Further resistance was pegged at $2.04-2.05.
Many traders said they expected a downward trend in cash prices ahead of the long holiday weekend to put pressure on May futures.
NYMEX's 12-month strip rose 0.3 cent to $2.066 as an estimated 19,495 Hub contracts traded as of 1530 EST. Open interest for March 25 rose 712 to 166,131.
NYMEX will suspend natgas futures trading this Friday in observance of the Good Friday holiday.

Following the release of American Gas Association data, May gained 1.1 cents to $1.894 in ACCESS. The storage data as of March 21 showed a stock decline of 54 bcf to 832 bcf or 26 percent of capacity.

Continued storage buying primarily in the southern plains and end-of-the-month balancing continued to support cash prices. Gulf swing prices were a few cents higher at $1.89-1.92 at the Henry Hub. April prices at the hub were little changed at $1.83-1.87 as some nomination deadlines had expired. Both swing and April prices on the Midco pipes were steady in the mid-to-high $1.70s and about $1.70-1.74, respectively. April Chicago city-gate was mostly at $1.94-1.95, while New York city-gate gas sold at $2.16-2.19 for next month, traders said.
Forecasts for the remainder of the week are calling for normal to above-normal temperatures across the U.S.

In the first week of April, temperatures are still expected to remain above normal in the Southwest and central plains, including Texas. Normal weather is forecast for the remainder of the U.S., except in the Northeast where temperatures are expected to be about two to four degrees Fahrenheit below normal.
No Permian or Alberta natgas futures traded. April Alberta futures rose three cents to $1.16.
On KCBT, May settled one cent higher at $1.71. Deferreds were flat to one cent higher. The East/West spread widened by 2.8 cents to 17.3 cents (NYMEX premium).
April cash prices in the Permian basin were fairly steady in the mid-$1.60s, while swing prices were talked higher at $1.74-1.79.
